title: Exec Readout — PLG→Sales Signal Pilot (Week 2)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
PLG→Sales Signal Pilot — Week 2 Exec Readout
Redwood Inference | 2025-03-07
Presenters: Chris Osei (Prod Ops), Grace O’Connor (SDR), Logan Wright (Eng)

Speaker notes:
- Purpose: share early signal quality + conversion, highlight wins/losses, propose threshold changes, and ask for rollout decision.


Slide 2 — Why we’re doing this
Goal: Turn self-serve product usage + intent into a consistent expansion motion (Dedicated/Private) with low false positives.
What “good” looks like:
- High-signal triggers that AEs/SDRs trust
- Fast + reliable routing into HubSpot with clear ownership + dedupe
- Measurable funnel: signal → outreach → meeting → SQL → pipeline → conversion

Speaker notes:
- Week 2 is still “learning mode,” but early data suggests we can tighten thresholds and reduce noise.


Slide 3 — Pilot scope (Week 1–2)
Cohort:
- 52 companies (self-serve), selected across NA + EMEA
- Suppressed: existing active opps, enterprise CSM-managed accounts, explicit opt-outs
Signals enabled (v1):
- Sustained spend growth (7/14/30d)
- Rate-limit pain (429s) + repeated quota friction
- Concurrency/throughput spikes (burst)
- Security intent (docs + console events)
- Region/residency intent (EU data residency docs + region selection attempts)
Routing:
- HubSpot company timeline event + task
- SDR sequence enrollment (where eligible)
- Slack notifications (#sales) only for highest-intent scores (>= “P1”)

Speaker notes:
- We intentionally started with a smaller cohort to tune dedupe, suppression, and copy before scaling.


Slide 4 — What shipped / is live
Data + scoring:
- 7/14/30d aggregations live (spend, tokens, concurrency, 429s, error-rate) with daily refresh
- Scoring service emits idempotent “signal events” (company-level)
GTM activation:
- HubSpot: company timeline event + task creation + auto-enroll sequence (where not suppressed)
- Slack: P1 signal notifications to #sales with HubSpot link
Operational guardrails:
- Cooldown window per company per signal type
- Dedupe keys + write-audit logs for HubSpot sync

Speaker notes:
- Main “new” this week: dedupe fix + more conservative cooldown for rate-limit signals (to prevent spam).


Slide 5 — Week 2 topline funnel (cumulative)
Definitions:
- “Raw events” = all signal emissions
- “Unique companies” = post-dedupe (company_id + signal_type + cooldown)
- “Actioned” = SDR sent email/LI or AE reached out

Cumulative totals (Weeks 1–2):
- Raw signal events: 118
- Dedupe / suppression removed: 54
- Unique companies surfaced: 64
- HubSpot tasks created: 46
- Enrolled in SDR sequences: 39
- Actioned within SLA (<= 2 biz days): 32 (70% of tasks)
- Meetings booked: 9
- SQLs created: 3
- Early pipeline created (unweighted): ~$420K

Speaker notes:
- The gap between “unique companies surfaced” and “tasks created” is almost entirely suppression rules + missing domain matching for a handful (see slide on data quality).


Slide 6 — Breakdown by signal type (Weeks 1–2)
Sustained spend growth:
- Unique companies: 18
- Meetings booked: 3
- Common outcome: Dedicated sizing conversation / commit discussion

Rate-limit pain (429s + quota friction):
- Unique companies: 21
- Meetings booked: 4
- Common outcome: Dedicated PoC request, batching/caching tuning, quota review

Concurrency / burst:
- Unique companies: 9
- Meetings booked: 2
- Common outcome: Dedicated capacity + latency SLO review

Security intent:
- Unique companies: 11
- Meetings booked: 2 (security review)
- Common outcome: SSO/SAML + audit logs + SOC2 questions; often maps to Private or Dedicated (w/ enterprise controls)

Region/residency intent:
- Unique companies: 5
- Meetings booked: 1
- Common outcome: EMEA routing, EU region feasibility, timeline alignment

Speaker notes:
- Rate-limit pain is the highest meeting generator so far, but also the biggest false-positive source if thresholds are too low.


Slide 7 — Win story #1: Northstar AI (Hosted → Dedicated)
Signal(s):
- Sustained spend growth (30d) + repeated 429s over 5 days
- Concurrency spikes during weekday peak
What happened:
- Routed to AE + SDR task; meeting booked in 48 hours
- Discovery confirmed: latency SLO misses during peak + desire for predictable throughput
Outcome:
- Dedicated PoC scoped; success criteria drafted (throughput, p95 latency, spend predictability)
- Next step: 2-week PoC with weekly check-ins

Notes/Quotes (from call):
- “We can’t risk getting throttled during peak usage.”
- “We’d rather commit to capacity than fight rate limits.”

Speaker notes:
- This is the archetype we want: sustained usage + pain + urgency.


Slide 8 — Win story #2: BrightLedger (Security intent → Security review)
Signal(s):
- Security docs engagement (SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2) + “security questionnaire” event
What happened:
- SDR outreach framed around timelines + evidence packet
- Security review booked; procurement process started
Outcome:
- Active security checklist (SOC2 report request, audit log details, key management)
- Next step: SE + security team to join follow-up; determine Dedicated vs Private deployment requirement

Speaker notes:
- This signal is slower to convert to “pipeline,” but it’s high leverage for enterprise readiness.


Slide 9 — Win story #3: OrbitDesk (Rate limits → PoC tuning)
Signal(s):
- Repeated 429s + latency complaints in support context
What happened:
- Signal routed + support context shared (avoiding user-level details)
- SE scheduled deep dive on batching/caching and quota
Outcome:
- Identified misconfigured burst pattern + lack of request batching
- Customer saw improvement after tuning; evaluating Dedicated if peak traffic continues

Speaker notes:
- Important: We have to keep “outreach” aligned with support/CS to avoid conflicting messages.


Slide 10 — Losses / false positives (what we learned)
Observed false-positive patterns (Week 1–2):
1) Short-lived spikes (demo days, launch test) that don’t persist
- Signal fired on 7d window; customer not actually scaling
2) “No budget / student / open-source eval” traffic
- High tokens but low willingness to commit; wrong motion
3) Rate-limit signals from client-side retry storms
- Not a capacity issue; often SDK retry config
4) Security intent from generic browsing
- One-off docs visits without procurement intent

Impact:
- Estimated false-positive rate (manual sampling of 25 surfaced companies): 28%
- Main driver: rate-limit signal thresholds too sensitive + missing “persistence” filter

Speaker notes:
- The goal isn’t zero false positives; it’s getting below ~15–20% while keeping volume high enough to matter.


Slide 11 — Data quality + operational issues
Issue A: Duplicate outreach (SUP-1932)
- Root cause: dedupe key mismatch when company domain mapping updated mid-day
- Fix: idempotency key normalized; cooldown enforced before task creation
- Status: fixed + verified in prod (ref: redwood/pr_9827)

Issue B: HubSpot matching gaps (domain → company record)
- A few companies lacked clean domain metadata; tasks weren’t created
- Mitigation: enrichment step (domain normalization) + fallback “create company” disabled for pilot (by design)

Issue C: SLA adherence (actioning tasks)
- 70% actioned within 2 business days; misses mainly due to unclear ownership + SDR bandwidth
- Mitigation: tighter routing rules + “P1 only” Slack to reduce distraction

Speaker notes:
- Dedupe stability is table stakes. We should not expand cohort size until we’re confident duplicates are contained.


Slide 12 — Copy + cadence feedback (from SDRs/AEs)
What’s working:
- Referencing concrete observed pain (429s, latency spikes) increases reply rate
- Offering a “5-min triage” vs “sales call” improves conversion

What’s not working:
- Assumptions about customer infra stack (“on Kubernetes?”) triggered pushback
- Too much content in Email 1; needs 2-line clarity + 1 proof point

Changes made this week:
- Updated templates: fewer assumptions, more benchmarking offers (“we can share target throughput for X model sizes”)
- Added “opt-out / wrong person?” line to reduce annoyance

Speaker notes:
- SDR feedback aligns with what we saw in replies: short, specific, and respectful wins.


Slide 13 — Threshold changes proposed (v1.1)
Goal: reduce false positives from bursty usage and low-intent browsing while maintaining meeting volume.

Change 1: Sustained spend growth
- Before: >= $1.5K in last 30d OR >= 25% WoW growth (7d)
- Proposed: >= $2.5K in last 30d AND 2 consecutive weeks of growth (14d trend)

Change 2: Rate-limit pain (429)
- Before: >= 10 429s/day on 2 days in 7d
- Proposed: >= 25 429s/day on 3 days in 7d OR (>= 15/day + concurrency spike)
- Add filter: exclude known retry-storm signature (high retry ratio)

Change 3: Security intent
- Before: any 1 security doc event
- Proposed: 2+ distinct security artifacts within 7d (e.g., SOC2 + SSO + audit logs) OR “security questionnaire” event

Change 4: Pricing-page intent (new scoring input, not standalone)
- Proposed: pricing page visits add score only when paired with usage pain (spend/429/concurrency)

Speaker notes:
- These are tuned to cut the noisy edge cases while keeping the “real pain + growth” cases.


Slide 14 — Rollout gates (what we propose to measure before expanding)
We recommend expanding cohort size only if we hit:
- Duplicate outreach incidents: 0 P0/P1 in 7 days
- False-positive rate: <= 20% (manual sample weekly) trending down
- Time-to-task in HubSpot: p95 <= 2 hours from signal emission
- HubSpot write failure rate: < 1% daily (with retries)
- Actioning SLA: >= 80% of tasks actioned within 2 biz days (or explicit reason logged)

Speaker notes:
- If any gate misses, we hold rollout and fix pipeline/rules first.


Slide 15 — Risks / things to watch
Privacy / trust:
- Keep signals company-level; avoid user-level identifiers in HubSpot/Slack
- Clear opt-out handling; suppress immediately on request

Organizational:
- Overlapping motions (support/CS vs SDR) can create confusion
- Need consistent logging of outcomes for KPI attribution

Technical:
- HubSpot API limits at higher volumes; batching + backoff OK so far
- Score drift as product changes (new tiers, quotas, regions)

Speaker notes:
- The biggest risk is “noise” hurting trust—both for customers and the sales team.


Slide 16 — Decision ask (Exec)
Ask #1: Approve v1.1 threshold changes + continue pilot through Week 4
- Implement proposed thresholds and retry-storm filter
- Keep cohort at 52 while we validate reduction in false positives

Ask #2: Conditional expansion plan (starting Week 4)
- Expand to 200 self-serve companies (top usage cohorts), IF rollout gates are met
- Enable EMEA routing + region/residency play (coordinate with Lukas Meyer)

Ask #3: Resource alignment
- Allocate 0.5–1.0 SE FTE equivalent for Dedicated PoC scoping from signals
- SDR bandwidth: ensure P1 signals get acted within SLA (reduce “nice to have” outbound)

Speaker notes:
- We’re not asking to scale to everyone yet—just approval to iterate thresholds and a clear “if gates met, then scale” path.


Slide 17 — Appendix: Week 2 raw examples (sanitized)
Example: Rate-limit + spend combo (good)
- 429s: 40–70/day for 4 days; spend up 35% WoW; concurrency peak tripled
- Outcome: meeting booked, Dedicated PoC scoped

Example: Rate-limit only (bad)
- 429s: 12/day for 2 days; spend flat; retry ratio extremely high
- Outcome: not a sales motion; fix SDK retry settings; no follow-up

Example: Security browsing (bad)
- Single visit to SOC2 page; no other signals; no reply
- Outcome: should not have triggered outreach in v1.1

Speaker notes:
- Including these examples helps calibrate intuition across Sales/Eng/Product about what “good” looks like.
